Every document is reviewed by two models from different providers, each given the document and
instructed to refute it, each blind to the other. Output is constrained to a schema, validated
before it is accepted, and turned into a published verdict by the fixed rule in
`build/audit/adjudicate.py`.

Reviews are published whole. That includes the findings the rule downgraded, the ones the
reviewers disagreed about, and the ones that blocked a document this project had already
invested a day in.

## The rule

| rule | what it does | why |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | A fatal or major finding that names no section, or states no fix, is downgraded to minor | A severe objection that cannot be acted on is an impression, not a finding. Downgrading keeps it visible at the weight it earned |
| R2 | Coverage is stated, never assumed | One returned verdict cannot produce agreement, and calling it agreement is the failure this process exists to prevent |
| R3 | An unrebutted fatal finding carrying a verbatim quote blocks the document, whatever the votes say | A quote from the document is a fact about the document; a vote is a judgment about it |
| R4 | Reviewers who disagree produce `contested`, not a winner | The disagreement is the information |

Rule version 1, pinned by twelve golden cases in `tests/test_adjudicate.py`. A rule is changed
only when a case fails under the old rule and passes under the new one, and both directions
have been checked.

## Verdicts

| verdict | meaning |
|---|---|
| `sound` | no finding above minor |
| `changes-required` | findings at major stand, none fatal survived |
| `contested` | reviewers disagreed and neither side settled it |
| `unsound` | every reviewer that voted judged it unsound |
| `blocked` | an evidenced fatal finding stands unrebutted |
| `no-verdict` | every reviewer abstained |

## What review has cost so far

The first document reviewed was blocked, on two fatal findings that were verified against
primary source and are correct. One of them is that the protocol had already looked at its own
outcome before claiming to be confirmatory. That is the second time in this project the same
class of error occurred, the first having been the reason the protocol was written at all.

A review process that never blocks anything is not a review process.
